note: Audit leads from official reports. These are not independent legal conclusions.

leads.title: Large cash prize withdrawals lacked documentation and monitoring
leads.summary: The city auditor reported significant cash withdrawals for prize distribution without adequate documentation, segregation of duties, oversight, or verification. The reported risk includes misappropriation, theft, loss of public funds, compliance issues, and tax-reporting problems.

leads.title: Purchases were made before requisitions and purchase orders
leads.summary: Auditors found numerous instances where invoice dates came before purchase requisitions or purchase orders, meaning purchases occurred before proper authorization. The risk noted includes unauthorized spending, budget overruns, noncompliance, fraud or abuse exposure, and possible financial misstatement.

leads.title: Unresolved cash variances and unreconciled accounts continued
leads.source: Miami FY 2023/24 Audit, Finding 2024-4 and FY 2022/23 Finding 2023-001
leads.summary: The FY 2023/24 audit repeated the prior cash-monitoring finding. FY 2022/23 cited a duplicate $78,000 cash-transfer entry and roughly a $128,000 variance between general-ledger cash and the adjusted bank-reconciliation balance.

leads.title: Federal reporting and procurement records were weak
leads.summary: The city did not timely monitor CSLFRF reporting requirements and lacked a centralized grant/reporting schedule. Procurement testing also found missing evidence of required public notice for 1 of 5 CSLFRF projects tested; questioned costs were listed as $0.

leads.title: Ottawa County audits report unsupported or improperly charged disbursements
leads.source: Ottawa County FY 2022, FY 2021, and FY 2020 audit findings
leads.summary: FY 2022 reported $1,162,112 lacking adequate support, $1,125,000 not made for the proper amount, $1,133,179 charged to the wrong period, and an $80,000 vendor payment not approved by BOCC/management. FY 2021 reported $493,602 lacking adequate support and $927,010 charged to the wrong fund/account. FY 2020 reported $643,657 without invoice support, $913,872 charged to the wrong fund, and $1,429,235 not encumbered before goods or services.

leads.title: Cash-bond documentation gaps create misappropriation risk
leads.source: Ottawa County FY 2022 and FY 2021 audit findings
leads.summary: The county could not provide adequate documentation to confirm that all cash bonds were deposited and paid out to the Court Clerk or arresting agency. Auditors identified inaccurate/incomplete records and misappropriation risk.

leads.title: Inmate Trust and Sheriff Commissary controls were not reliable
leads.summary: The FY 2022 audit reported missing daily deposits, missing logs, incomplete reconciliations, account closures without supporting documentation, no timely commissary annual report to BOCC, and bank activity suggesting a vendor deposited into the Inmate Trust account.

leads.title: CSLFRF allowability could not be determined for an $80,000 disbursement
leads.summary: Auditors tested all $1,326,325 in CSLFRF expenditures. Because a warrant was canceled and reissued to a different vendor without a new purchase order, auditors could not determine whether one $80,000 disbursement was allowable.
